synonyms: Clematis dioica var. drummondii (Torr. & A.Gray) Kuntze
taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO and Flora of North America.

evidence: Hays — UT Plant Resources Center Flora of Purola Preserve explicitly lists Clematis drummondii among naturally occurring plants of northern Hays County.
Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Ranunculaceae herbarium index includes multiple Clematis drummondii specimens.
Williamson — UT Plant Resources Center Vascular Plants of Williamson County provides a detailed native field treatment for Clematis drummondii.
target_zone_range.guardrail: No county inferred from statewide range, ecoregion, cultivation, plant sales, or an unreconciled historical taxonomic concept.

morphology.look_here_first: Look at the flower architecture and sex first: small open white-to-cream flowers with four spreading sepals occur on separate male and female vines; later, female plants explode into masses of long silky plumose seed tails.
diagnostic_traits: woody scrambling/climbing vine, often several meters
opposite odd-pinnate leaves, usually 5-foliolate with deeply divided or cleft leaflets
four thin white-to-cream sepals spread flat rather than forming a leathery urn
male flowers with many stamens; female flowers with many pistils
achenes with very long 4–9 cm plumose beaks forming conspicuous 'old man's beard' masses

confusers.separator: Both can look white-flowered at a glance, but C. drummondii is dioecious with more deeply divided leaflets and relatively few larger open flowers; C. terniflora has masses of small bisexual white flowers and mostly entire 3–5-foliolate leaves.
C. pitcheri has nodding thick-sepaled purple leathery urns; C. drummondii has thin white spreading sepals and no urn-shaped flower.
